items.content:
내면 지도 그리기_ 우리가 바라는 행운

숨은 보물은 왜 늘 같은 모양이어야 할까

선생님은 늘 “이 보물을 찾으세요” 하고 모양과 크기를 알려주었지요.

대개는 작게 접힌 하얀 쪽지였고, 가끔은 색종이나 번호표 같은 것이었습니다.

하지만 그 놀이의 숨은 규칙은 거기 있었는지도 모릅니다.

보물을 찾기 전에, 이미 보물의 모양을 먼저 배웠다는 것.

이렇게 생긴 것, 이 정도 크기, 이런 색.

그러니 발밑에 다른 것이 있어도 쉽게 지나쳤습니다.

지금 우리가 행운을 꿈꾸는 방식도 조금 비슷해 보입니다.

행운을 찾고 싶어 하지만, 그보다 먼저 행운의 모양부터 너무 좁게 정해두는 건 아닌가 싶을 때가 있습니다.

수익이 나야 하고, 숫자로 보이고, 남들도 부러워해야 하고, 눈에 띄게 상승해야 한다고 믿는 식으로 말입니다.

예전에는 돈을 번다는 말이 다소 멀게 느껴졌다면, 지금은 손안의 앱과 짧은 뉴스, 누군가의 후기와 알림 몇 개만으로도 행운이 아주 가까운 데 있는 것처럼 느껴집니다.

기회는 빠르게 지나가고, 결정은 즉시 해야되고, 불안은 뒤늦게 오지 않고 실시간으로 옵니다.

투자는 미래를 준비하는 일일 수도 있지만, 어느 순간부터는 오늘의 마음을 들쑤시는 일이 되기도 합니다.

행운은 아직 오지 않았는데, 놓칠까 봐 조급해지는 마음만 먼저 도착하는 것 처럼요.

한편에서는 AI가 나타나 취직과 이직, 성장과 생존의 문법을 바꾸고 있습니다.

어제까지의 성실함이 오늘의 경쟁력을 보장하지 못하고,

어제까지의 경력이 내일의 안전을 약속하지 못합니다.

어떻게든 나를 지키려고 강연을 듣고, 책을 읽고, AI 설명서를 뒤적이고, 커뮤니티를 헤맵니다.

뒤처지지 않기 위해서이기도 하고, 무엇보다 대체되지 않기 위해서입니다.

이 시대의 불안은 가난만이 아니라, 대체 가능성의 공포니까요.

그럴 때면 한 작가의 말을 떠올립니다.

“작가가 된 후 복권은 사지 않는다. 모든 행운이 내가 쓴 책에 몰아지길 바라는 마음에서.”

이 문장을 되새길 때 마다 뭉클해집니다.

그 말 속에는 단순한 절제나 금욕이 아니라, 삶에 대한 아주 선명한 편애가 들어 있기 때문입니다.

행운이 오더라도 다른 데 새지 말고, 내가 가장 귀하게 여기는 일 위에 내려앉았으면 좋겠다는 마음.

어쩌면 그 말은 행운을 바라는 것이 아니라,

무엇을 행운이라고 부를지 스스로 정했다는 결심에 더 가까우니까요.

심리학에서는 사람들이 대개 손실을 이익보다 더 크게 느낀다고 하죠. 같은 액수라도 버는 기쁨보다 잃는 고통이 더 오래 가고, 그래서 우리는 자꾸 놓친 행운을 돌아봅니다.

하지만 가만히 생각해보면, 우리가 놓쳤다고 여기는 것들 중 적지 않은 수는 사실 잡았더라면 다른 종류의 불안을 데려왔을지도 모릅니다. 밤마다 차트를 확인하게 만드는 돈, 사람을 더 조급하게 만드는 수익, 잠깐의 환호 뒤에 더 큰 갈증을 남기는 상승. 그것을 정말 행운이라고만 부를 수 있을까요.

돈은 귀합니다. 이 사실을 점잖게 부정할 필요는 없습니다.

다만 돈이 늘 행운의 얼굴만 하고 오지는 않는다는 것도 알아야 합니다.

어떻게 벌었는지, 무엇을 잃으며 지켰는지, 얼마를 손에 쥐었는데도 왜 계속 불안한지까지 함께 보아야 합니다. 어떤 돈은 사람을 살리고, 어떤 돈은 사람을 갉아먹습니다. 어떤 성공은 어깨를 펴게 하고, 어떤 성공은 하루 종일 화면을 새로 고치게 만듭니다. 그러니 중요한 것은 얼마를 벌었는지 보다 그것이 내 삶을 어떤 모양으로 바꾸고 있는가일지도 모릅니다.

그런데 정말 바라는 것이 행운 자체인지, 아니면 내가 원하는 모양의 행운인지, 한 번쯤은 묻고 싶어집니다.

우리는 너무 자주 보물의 모양을 미리 정해둡니다.

크게 벌어야 하고, 빨리 올라야 하고, 남들도 부러워해야 하고, 숫자로 증명되어야 한다고 믿습니다.

어떤 사람에게 행운은 수익률일 것이고, 어떤 사람에게는 끝내 포기하지 않은 공부일 것이며, 어떤 사람에게는 아이와 먹는 저녁이고, 또 어떤 사람에게는 한 문장을 끝까지 쓰는 저녁일 것입니다.

그 작가에게 행운은 복권이 아니라 소설이었듯이,

운이 비켜가도 무너지지 않을 만큼, 내가 중요하다고 믿는 가치와 일상.

그러니 지금 필요한 것은 더 많은 행운의 정보가 아니라,

내가 무엇을 보물이라고 부를 것인지 다시 정하는 일인지도 모릅니다.

숨은 보물찾기에서 중요한 것은 빨리 찾는 능력만이 아니라,

보물의 모양을 함부로 하나로 정해두지 않는 상상력인지도 모릅니다.

당장 수익이 나지 않아도 보물일 수 있고,

남들이 탐내지 않아도 내 삶을 오래 지켜주는 것이라면

그것 역시 충분히 귀한 발견일 수 있습니다.

어쩌면 삶은 행운을 좇는 일이 아니라,

행운의 모습을 하고 다가오는 수많은 불운들 사이에서

내가 끝까지 사랑하고 싶은 것을 알아보는 일인지도 모릅니다.

아연(Ayn) ('서점여행자의 영감수업' 등 콘텐츠 기획)

items.title: Amazon CEO reportedly raised Anthropic model concerns before government crackdown
items.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy may have been the source of security concerns that led Anthropic to cut off worldwide access to two models on Friday.
items.content:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy may have been the source of security concerns that led Anthropic to cut off worldwide access to two models on Friday.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Jassy told Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other government officials that Amazon researchers used Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 to obtain information that could be used in cyberattacks. The government subsequently imposed an export control ban on the Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models.

An Amazon spokesperson said in a statement that while it’s “not uncommon for governments to seek our counsel on potential security risks,” the company does not “share the details of those discussions.”

The Information and Reuters similarly reported that Amazon (a major Anthropic investor ) had communicated concerns about the security of Anthropic’s models.

David Sacks, Trump’s former AI czar who now co-chairs the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, offered his own account of the discussions, claiming that “a highly credible trusted partner of both Anthropic and the USG […] came forward with [information about] a jailbreak.”

Sacks added, “The Admin asked [Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei] to fix the jailbreak or de-deploy the model. Dario refused.”

This post has been updated with a statement from an Amazon spokesperson.

items.title: OpenAI faces investigation from state attorneys general
items.summary: It's not clear which states are involved, but they're asking about everything from OpenAI's ad policies to its handling of health data.
items.content:
A coalition of state attorneys general has reportedly opened an investigation into OpenAI.

The company was served with a subpoena from New York’s attorney general on Friday , according to The Wall Street Journal. That subpoena sought documents related to a broad range of topics including the company’s advertising, user engagement and retention, model sycophancy, handling of consumer data and health data, and treatment of minors and seniors.

TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI and the New York attorney general’s office for confirmation. A company spokesperson told the WSJ that OpenAI is cooperating with the investigation.

“AI is a new and powerful technology, and we work every day to safely bring its benefits to people in a responsible way,” the spokesperson said in a statement. “We take the concerns raised by state attorneys general seriously and intend to engage constructively with their offices.”

According to Bloomberg , the spokesperson also said that ChatGPT now “includes a more protective experience for minors and people experiencing difficult situations, with safeguards that direct them to real-world resources and trusted human contacts.” The company declined to specify which states are involved in the investigation or to share more details about what information was requested.

OpenAI recently defeated its co-founder Elon Musk in a high-profile trial, after Musk accused the company of violating its founding agreement. (Musk’s lead attorney said he will appeal the decision.)

However, OpenAI still faces lawsuits over everything from alleged copyright infringement to ChatGPT’s alleged role in suicide . Earlier this month, Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier sued OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman , claiming that OpenAI and Altman “ignored internal and external safety warnings, put children at great risk, and allowed a dangerous product to reach millions of Floridians.”

Altman recently apologized to the community of Tumbler Ridge, Canada after a mass shooting; he acknowledged that OpenAI failed to alert law enforcement after the company flagged and banned the suspected shooter’s ChatGPT account.

The company announced this week that it has filed confidentially to go public .

items.title: Microsoft hasn’t ruled out spinning off Xbox
items.summary: Microsoft is preparing to lay off a significant chunk of its Xbox division and is reevaluating the plans for its next-generation Project Helix console. It's apparently also considering dramatically restructuring its relationship with Xbox, and hasn't ruled out spinning it off int
items.content:
Nothing is imminent, but nothing is off the table.

Microsoft is preparing to lay off a significant chunk of its Xbox division and is reevaluating the plans for its next-generation Project Helix console. It’s apparently also considering dramatically restructuring its relationship with Xbox, and hasn’t ruled out spinning it off into a separate company.

A new report from The Information suggests that Microsoft has considered some dramatic measures to make its Xbox unit more sustainable. That includes turning it into a wholly owned subsidiary, a joint venture, or even spinning it off entirely, with the possibility of selling the business. The report doesn’t suggest anything is imminent, but it does seem that new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella haven’t taken anything off the table when it comes to the future of Xbox.

Sharma has won approval to invest heavily in tentpole titles like Halo and Fallout. The former hasn’t seen a new release since 2021, and the last mainline Fallout title was Fallout 4 in 2015. She has also said that major upcoming releases Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution would be Xbox exclusive . Though this investment in its most popular franchises is likely to come at the expense of smaller studios and games that have failed to live up to sales expectations.

items.title: My first 24 hours with Siri AI on the Mac
items.summary: I turned off Siri on the Mac years ago and never looked back. Similarly, I found Apple Intelligence so fruitless I never engage with it. But the new Siri AI coming to macOS 27 Golden Gate has at least got me slightly rethinking things. I'm still early in testing Siri AI, as I've
items.content:
﻿Siri is better, but its limitations are much more obvious on a Mac than an iPhone.

I turned off Siri on the Mac years ago and never looked back. Similarly, I found Apple Intelligence so fruitless I never engage with it. But the new Siri AI coming to macOS 27 Golden Gate has at least got me slightly rethinking things.

I’m still early in testing Siri AI, as I’ve only had access to it in the macOS 27 developer beta for little more than 24 hours. It’s also in an early preview state on the dev beta, so there should be lots of runway for improvements before it releases later this year. I don’t even know if it’s done indexing my files and folders on our review unit M5 MacBook Air and M5 Max MacBook Pro . Unlike on the iOS 27 dev beta, there’s no “indexing in progress” box in the settings page. I asked Siri if it could tell me, but it told me to click a button in Settings that isn’t there.

My colleagues got a headstart testing Siri AI on the iPhone and Apple Watch , and getting a read on its general vibe , and they’ve so far had some positive feedback from using it. My feelings are a little more mixed.

When I sit down at a laptop I don’t need a voice assistant for searching things I’m randomly curious about or checking the weather like I would on a phone; I can do that faster and more accurately with keyboard and mouse. So I tried to think of ways to let Siri AI help me on macOS — things that might actually be useful to me in my everyday work.

I’d be happy to automate some of the time-consuming benchmarking I do when reviewing laptops, but although Siri AI can launch apps, it can’t take actions inside them (not that Apple ever claimed it could). I then tried to see if vibe coding a couple Shortcuts could get me there instead. This isn’t a Siri AI feature, but it is a new part of Apple Intelligence. I asked Shortcuts to run a test in either Geekbench or Cinebench, capture the results in a screenshot, wait a few minutes, and repeat the process two more times. But the resulting automations couldn’t actually run the tests either. Apple Intelligence made a shortcut that opened Geekbench and took screenshots (but forgot about actually running the benchmark), and it made a Cinebench shortcut that had “Wait for you to run the test” as an actual step. Maybe if developers continue expanding App Intents this could one day work.

So if Siri can’t help me run my benchmarks, maybe it can at least help me be a little faster in logging the data. In my normal workflow, I run each benchmark three times, taking screenshots as I go, and later average out the results before cataloging them in a spreadsheet. Apple’s WWDC keynote showed someone using Ask Siri in Spotlight to analyze data in local files. So I tried selecting batches of those screenshots in Finder and asking Siri to calculate the average scores for me. It worked pretty well — most of the time.

It was smart enough to distinguish single-core CPU scores from multicore CPU scores and GPU scores, average the test results, and arrange them in easy-to-read tables. But it could get thrown off if I included screenshots of too many different types of tests, especially if I mixed ones with synthetic score results (Geekbench, PugetBench, etc.) and time-based results (Blender render tests and our 4K video export test). And it sometimes got thrown off by the CPU rankings data that’s visible in Cinebench screenshots. Ideally, I’d be able to have Siri AI accurately calculate the 15 or so averages from my dozens of screenshots all at once — that would save me some serious time. But for now, it can at best only help me a little bit. And unless it gets better I’m still inclined to continue doing it all myself, especially since Siri messed up the numbers a couple times by pulling the wrong data.

So far, Siri AI seems a lot more capable within Apple’s ecosystem than it is outside of it, even for apps and files that are already on my Mac but in non-Apple apps. When I asked Siri to find my pictures of cats or babies, it pulled up results from Apple’s Photos and Messages apps. This could be enough for plenty of people, but not for me. Most of my messaging is done in Signal, and photos from my phone are uploaded to Google Photos, not iCloud. Siri also missed the thousands of images I have in my Lightroom Classic catalog, even though the files are stored locally in the Pictures folder and I kept asking it to access them directly. It’s possible those files haven’t been indexed yet, but I have no way to tell.

For now, I’m getting similar vibes to when I tested Copilot Vision last year . Like Copilot Vision, you can use Siri’s Visual Intelligence to ask questions about things on your screen. And like Copilot, it’s limited. I asked Siri to evaluate benchmark results on a spreadsheet in Google Sheets, but it can’t see all the data if it’s not visible onscreen all at once. I could get it to see the whole spreadsheet by downloading it as an Excel file and pointing Siri at it in Finder, but when I asked for the laptop with the highest single-core Geekbench score it gave me multicore data. Not great.

I opened Siri while running Lightroom Classic, on a black-and-white photo from my Ricoh GR IV Monochrome review , and asked Siri how to make it look more like a shot from street photographer Alan Schaller . Siri offered specific value adjustments for exposure, contrast, and so on, and adjusting those values gave me a decent result. Unfortunately, when I asked Siri to judge the result, it went sycophant on me, saying I’d nailed the look and achieved an “almost timeless feel,” which is the type of behavior Apple says it’s not supposed to show. (I thought we were past this.)

Then I uploaded a classic Garry Winograd photo and asked how to change my Lightroom settings to match that photo; Siri recommended I set the exposure to the value it was already at. So, some hits and some misses.
